newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli CPI-linked and unlinked bonds rise.
newsitem.headline: Israeli CPI-linked and unlinked bonds rise.

text.p: Israeli CPI-linked and unlinked bonds closed higher on Tuesday, although traders said they were now more pessimistic about prospects for a cut in interest rates later this month.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.1 pct to 172.34
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 pct to 162.47
Volume was moderate at 156 million shekels with most of the activity concentrated in unlinked bonds and Makams.

"The market is mixed and there is no clear direction. Some believe that the Bank of Israel will lower its base rate for December by more than 0.5 percentage point, but others are less optimistic," said Danny Shamir of Israel Discount Bank.
"The M1 figure was relatively high and the Bank of Israel may decide to leave its short-term interest rate unchanged or lower it by only 0.5 percentage points," said Amitay Tafla of Sigma Securities.
The Bank of Israel said on Tuesday that M1 money supply grew a preliminary 0.4 percent in November, following a revised 1.5 percent decline in October,
"CPI-linked bonds rose today as the market expects only a minimal reduction in interest rates," Tafla said.

But Shamir said unlinked bonds also continued to rise because some investors still believe the central bank will lower the interest rate by more than 0.5 point. "I believe that these bonds are becoming risky," Shamir said.
Traders said despite the rise of unlinked bonds Makams posted only a moderate rise.
"Dollar-linked bonds closed lower for the first time after a few days of nice gains following the rise of the shekel against the dollar on Monday and Tuesday," Shamir added.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
